patient.name: Ethan Voss
patient.chiefComplaint: Abdominal pain and guarding; nonverbal, communicating distress through vocalizations and behavior only

history.hpi: Mother reports patient has been holding his abdomen, moaning, and refusing to eat since early afternoon, with unusual withdrawal from his normal routine and resistance to being touched near the stomach. No vomiting reported at home. No fever noted, though she did not take his temperature.
history.lastOralIntake: Small amount of breakfast around 8 AM; refused lunch
history.events: Mother noticed increasing abdominal guarding and unusual vocalizations over several hours and called 911 when patient refused to walk to the car for a scheduled appointment

scene.location: Single-family home, patient's bedroom, lying on his left side on the bed
scene.safety: No hazards noted; patient may be resistant to unfamiliar touch or environment changes
scene.bystanders: Mother present, primary caregiver and communication support; father en route
visualCues: Patient curled on his left side, knees drawn to chest
Grimacing and rocking, no verbal complaints
Mother gently stroking patient's arm using his usual calming routine
Abdomen visibly guarded when anyone approaches

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: 16-year-old male with autism spectrum disorder (nonverbal) presents curled on his side, guarding his abdomen, moaning and rocking. His mother is present and serves as primary historian and communication support.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, tachycardic, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all extremities, resists abdominal palpation
otherFindings: Abdomen rigid and guarded on approach
Curled in fetal position, will not straighten legs
Baseline nonverbal per mother; communicates via vocalizations, gestures, and behavior, not words
Increased rocking and hand movements consistent with mother's description of his pain behavior
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Nonverbal; moans and vocalizes distress, does not use words

transitions.if: History and FLACC pain score obtained
transitions.condition: Crew adapts its approach, obtains history primarily from the mother, and assesses pain using the FLACC observational scale given the patient's nonverbal, cognitively-impaired status.

phases.name: History and FLACC pain score obtained
phases.description: Crew slows its pace, follows the mother's guidance on approach, and completes a structured assessment using caregiver-reported history and an observational pain scale rather than a self-report scale.
phases.triggerCondition: Recognizing the patient cannot self-report pain, the crew gathers the history from his mother and scores pain using the FLACC observational scale as directed by protocol for patients with cognitive impairment unable to self-report.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, tachycardic, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Resists abdominal palpation, guards on approach
otherFindings: FLACC score 7/10 (grimacing face, legs drawn up, rigid activity, frequent vocalization, difficult to console)
Abdominal rigidity and voluntary guarding persist, worse in the right lower quadrant
No fever spike yet documented but temp trending up
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Nonverbal; moans and vocalizes distress, does not use words

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess pain using the FLACC observational scale (nonverbal/cognitive impairment)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Less than 4 years old or those with cognitive impairment unable to self-report: Observational Scales — Faces, Legs, Arms, Cry, Consolability (FLACC), Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario Pain Scale (CHEOPS)
expectedActions.rationale: The patient cannot use a numeric self-report scale; an observational tool is required for an accurate pain assessment.

expectedActions.shortAction: Obtain full vital signs (pulse, BP, RR, neurologic status)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Obtain vital signs including pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment
expectedActions.rationale: Establishes a baseline to trend response to treatment.

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess for signs of ischemic/perforated bowel: rigidity, distension, guarding, fever
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Signs and symptoms of ischemic, necrotic, or perforated bowel: Severe tenderness, Abdominal pain with motion or palpation of the abdomen, Fever, Abdominal distention, with tympany to percussion
expectedActions.rationale: Rigid, guarded abdomen with low-grade fever raises concern for a surgical abdomen.

expectedActions.shortAction: Obtain vascular access to allow analgesia administration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Obtain vascular access as necessary to provide analgesia and/or fluid resuscitation
expectedActions.rationale: Prepares for weight-based analgesia once the pain assessment is complete.

transitions.condition: Based on the FLACC score indicating severe pain, the crew administers weight-based analgesia despite the patient's inability to verbally rate pain, consistent with protocol guidance that acute abdominal pain should be treated with analgesia.
Crew misattributes the patient's rocking, vocalizing, and resistance to touch as baseline autistic behavior rather than a pain response, skips a structured pain assessment, and withholds analgesia.

phases.name: FLACC-guided analgesia given
phases.description: Crew administers intranasal fentanyl dosed to the patient's weight, choosing the IN route to avoid a distressing IV attempt, then prepares for transport.
phases.triggerCondition: The FLACC score of 7/10 indicates severe pain despite the patient's outwardly calm baseline; per protocol, acute abdominal pain should be treated with analgesia, so the crew proceeds with weight-based opioid analgesia via the intranasal route.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, improving, skin less diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Tolerates gentle palpation better than on arrival
otherFindings: Guarding still present but less rigid
Mother reports patient calmer, rocking less frequent
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Nonverbal; vocalizations quieter and less distressed

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 65 mcg IN (65 kg × 1 mcg/kg; max 100 mcg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: IN route avoids a distressing IV attempt in a patient who may not tolerate unfamiliar procedures well.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess FLACC pain score and vital signs after analgesia
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Documentation of patient reassessment with repeat vital signs and patient pain scale assessment
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms the analgesia is working and screens for early respiratory depression.

expectedActions.shortAction: Position of comfort; minimize unfamiliar stimulation per mother's guidance
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Non-pharmacologic pain management options include Placement of the patient in a position of comfort ... Verbal reassurance to control anxiety
expectedActions.rationale: Reduces additional distress on top of the medical intervention.

transitions.condition: With pain improving and vitals trending toward baseline, crew packages the patient with his mother accompanying for continuity of communication and prepares for transport.

phases.name: Transport initiated with mother present
phases.description: Patient is transported with his mother present to support communication and comfort; crew continues serial reassessment en route given the persistent abdominal rigidity concerning for a surgical abdomen.
phases.triggerCondition: Analgesia and a calm, caregiver-guided approach have reduced distress; crew proceeds to transport with continued reassessment.

otherFindings: Abdominal guarding persists though less severe
Mother remains at bedside throughout transport

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to appropriate receiving facility; reassess vitals and pain en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Provide transport to an appropriate receiving facility. Reassess vital signs and response to therapeutic interventions throughout transport
expectedActions.rationale: Persistent rigidity warrants ongoing reassessment for a surgical abdomen despite improved comfort.

phases.name: FLACC skipped, pain untreated
phases.description: Without a structured pain assessment, the patient's distress escalates — increased rocking, resistance to touch, and rising heart rate — making the abdominal exam harder to trust and delaying recognition of his true pain level.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew interprets the patient's rocking, vocalizing, and resistance to touch as his baseline autistic behavior rather than a pain response, skips an observational pain assessment, and does not administer analgesia.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, tachycardic, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Increased self-restraint against touch, harder to examine
otherFindings: Increased rocking and resistance to touch
Mother reports this is worse than his usual baseline, not just typical behavior
Abdominal exam limited by patient's escalating distress
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Nonverbal; louder, more frequent distress vocalizations

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize escalating distress as undertreated pain; FLACC score and fentanyl 65 mcg IN
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Observational Scales — Faces, Legs, Arms, Cry, Consolability (FLACC) ... Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: Undertreated pain compounds the patient's distress and makes ongoing assessment less reliable the longer it goes unaddressed.
